issues.title: Collect and audit a small real-teacher demonstration pilot
issues.body:
## Outcome
Produce the first audited real-teacher training demonstrations and estimate yield and cost before committing to a larger corpus.

## Dependencies
- [ ] #19 — Evaluate one real LLM on 20–30 procurement development cases and triage failures

Dependencies are explicit issue links, not native GitHub blocking relationships. Preparation may proceed against agreed contracts, but dependent execution waits for acceptance evidence. PR #16 is currently open and unmerged.

## Deliverables
Versioned teacher-pilot manifest, verified train-only JSONL, rejection/coverage audit, source/provider-use record and cost-per-accepted-episode estimate.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Use the development evaluation findings to choose a teacher and document provider/source terms, permitted output use, model/configuration, task mix, collection size and spend ceiling before running.
- [ ] Collect only on training lineages; preserve separate development and sealed evaluation cases and exclude answer keys from teacher input.
- [ ] Replay and independently verify every admitted demonstration; keep failed and partial attempts separate with diagnostic reasons.
- [ ] Audit a stratified subset for unsupported assumptions, shortcuts, valid uncertainty handling and business realism; record actual review status.
- [ ] Validate export compatibility, assistant-only loss targets, provenance, deduplication and leakage checks.
- [ ] Report attempted versus accepted counts, post-filter difficulty/coverage, provider tokens and total cost per accepted episode; avoid claiming training benefit before an experiment.
- [ ] Record whether to expand collection, improve diversity, repair tasks, or stop. No bulk generation or fine-tuning execution is included.

## Completion evidence
Link the implementing PR/review record, reproducible checks, sanitized raw logs and actual screenshots. Update progress.md and the parent epic after accepted work. Do not claim practitioner review, paid model results, or learning gains without evidence.

## Scope and controls
Initial domain: discrete manufacturing and distribution, supplier allocation. Keep credentials and case-level evaluation evidence outside the public repository. No assignee, deadline, provider choice or spend approval is implied.

Parent: #1. Follow-on planning: #12 and #14.

Preregistered development run manifest, private trajectories, sanitized scorecard, cost report, failure taxonomy and scoped corrective issues.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Record practitioner readiness decision, exact model/provider version, tool profile, prompts, action/token limits, retry rules, repeated-run sampling and approved spend ceiling.

- [ ] Make a go/repair/stop recommendation for teacher collection; 20–30 cases are diagnostic and do not establish broad capability or a stable leaderboard.

issues.title: Implement a real-LLM adapter with fixed tool profile, budgets and telemetry
issues.body:
## Outcome
Allow one selected real LLM to act through the existing environment tools with the same observable information boundary as the offline agent.

## Dependencies
- [ ] #9 — Agent runner (implementation in PR #16)
- [ ] #7 — Private evaluation boundaries (implementation in PR #16)

Dependencies are explicit issue links, not native GitHub blocking relationships. Preparation may proceed against agreed contracts, but dependent execution waits for acceptance evidence. PR #16 is currently open and unmerged.

## Deliverables
Provider adapter, recorded model/configuration contract, offline mocked integration tests and a budgeted live connectivity check when configured.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Select an initial provider/model explicitly and record exact model ID, prompt, tool schemas, memory, retry/timeout policy and token/action limits.
- [ ] Implement real provider requests and tool-call/result translation through the existing runner; expose no World truth, expected outcome, reference solution or private grader to the adapter.
- [ ] Handle malformed calls, rate limits, retries, refusals, context limits and incomplete episodes without fabricating success or usage.
- [ ] Load credentials from an approved secret mechanism; redact secrets from trajectories and public reports.
- [ ] Track actual calls, token usage, latency and cost; enforce a configured monetary ceiling and report unknown costs honestly.
- [ ] Pass mocked offline tests without credentials; perform a small live connectivity check only once credentials, model choice and an explicit spend ceiling are recorded.
- [ ] Record tests, raw sanitized logs and actual screenshot evidence. No paid evaluation is authorized by issue creation alone.

## Completion evidence
Link the implementing PR/review record, reproducible checks, sanitized raw logs and actual screenshots. Update progress.md and the parent epic after accepted work. Do not claim practitioner review, paid model results, or learning gains without evidence.

## Scope and controls

pull_requests.title: Build verified episode pipeline and run 100-case offline smoke experiment
pull_requests.head: 451788d1a2527256c8abd67b34467bbabb2cd0ff
pull_requests.body:
Adds the pipeline from generated procurement situations to verified training demonstrations: lineage/private boundaries (#7), varied task generation (#8), visible-input agent runner (#9), replay admission/train-only JSONL export (#10), and offline smoke execution (#11).

Actual experiment: 100 cases (60 train /20 development /20 evaluation), 634 tool actions, 100 checker/admission passes and replays, 60 training exports, 40 protected records filtered, and three corrupted-hash probes rejected. Zero provider calls, tokens or charges. All private case-level artifacts, fixed seed and evaluation records stay outside this public repository.

Validation: 57 local tests pass, including independent regressions for forged splits/ancestry, replay tampering, injected hidden metadata and repairs that drop demand. Six GPT-6.1 Sol agents planned/built/reviewed. Per-issue plans, reports, raw output and seven actual Chromium screenshots: [batch 2 proof](https://github.com/kishorkukreja/SupplyChainWorld/blob/implementation/verified-episode-pipeline/evidence/batch2.md).

The offline scripted agent optimizes only visible records; these results validate integration, not LLM ability or fine-tuning gains. Only three split-specific synthetic lineage templates are represented; practitioner review pending. In-process agent isolation is not a hostile-code sandbox, timeout is cooperative, solver is small-instance bounded enumeration, infeasibility certificates cover capacity.

Closes #7
Closes #8
Closes #9
Closes #10
Closes #11

Remote CI should be checked on this head before merge.

pull_requests.body:
Implements the first procurement prototype for issues #2, #3, #4, #5 and #6: ten synthetic reference cases, validated contracts, independent business checking, bounded exact solver/heuristic, and a resettable typed environment.

Six GPT-6.1 Sol agents planned, built and reviewed the work. Plans/results for every issue and seven real Chromium screenshots are in [evidence/README.md](evidence/README.md). Raw logs include commands, timestamps, exit status and output hashes. The screenshots show recorded verification reports, not a product UI.

Validation: 26 local unittest tests passed. Independent checks exercised all ten cases through submission/replay/reset and verified fixed fees across multiple items. Remote CI is configured but has not been observed passing yet.

Limits: all fixtures are synthetic; practitioner review pending. Exact enumeration is limited to small reference instances. Infeasibility checking currently certifies capacity shortfalls. No paid model runs, fine-tuning, private dataset release or broad capability claims. Issues stay open for acceptance review.

Next work after acceptance: #7 lineage/privacy controls, then generation/runner work according to dependencies.
